newsitem.title: UK: Green diesel change leaves IPE gas oil vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: Green diesel change leaves IPE gas oil vulnerable.

text.p: October's change in the sulphur content of European diesel may make IPE gas oil futures more vulnerable to being cornered, European traders said on Friday.

The European gas oil pool, which was until now 0.2 percent sulphur for both heating oil and diesel, will be split into about 60 percent 0.2 percent for heating oil and 40 percent 0.05 percent sulphur for diesel.
The IPE contract will continue to specify only 0.2 percent.

This means that any attempt by one trader to corner the 0.2 sulphur market in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area, as occurred earlier this year, would require a smaller position on the futures market to succeed, traders said.
"The risk has always been there, but clearly it has increased with the change of specs," a leading gas oil trader said.
IPE official Trevor Christmas said there was no sign that any traders were attempting to build up abnormally large positions on the September contract ahead of its expiry on September 12.
But traders said the changes could increase the risk of market distortions through a big delivery.
Dealers said that if deliveries into the IPE contract return to their January peak of 850,000 tonnes this winter, there could be a shortage of 0.2 percent material to cover it.
However, others noted that a large delivery of 0.2 percent fuel would require sufficient local demand to merit it, because IPE deliveries cannot be loaded directly on to cargo vessels for export.

As a preventive measure, the IPE has monitored its members' positions since early this year. In addition, 0.05 percent fuel can be delivered into the IPE contract if 0.2 percent runs short, although traders may be reluctant to do this with the current $10 per tonne premium for 0.05 over 0.2.
"You could have low sulphur delivered into the screen in an extreme backwardation," a trader said.
The IPE met earlier this year to discuss the issue of European diesel and decided that its contract should use only heating oil as its underlying commodity, Christmas added.
